chapter: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
title: Writing "Epistrophy" with Monk after fooling with Charlie's tipple
summary: Clarke worked out "Epistrophy" from notes on a tipple in his hotel room; Monk supplied the last two bars, and the tune did not make them rich.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It's unbelievable. Because it's his music. 'Round About Midnight.' Well, we wrote 'Epistrophy' (PHONETIC) together. Now, 'Epistrophy', Charlie and I were in my hotel room, playing around with the ukulele, you know. Well, Charlie could play any stringed instrument he picked up, he could play it. I don't care what it is. So this dancer had this old ukulele, you know, a tipple they call it.
You know, it's sort of a mandolin, but --
-- two strings. So -- two strings on each pivot, you know.

So we -- he dropped it on the bed, so Charlie began to play it, but really play it. So then Charlie put it down and they began talking, so I picked it up, and I said, 'Doo-de, doo-de,' so I began to figure out what notes -- because I didn't know the notes on the tipple, you know. I said, 'Now, what notes could these be?' So I said, 'Well, maybe it's C-sharp and D, maybe.' So I said, well it's a half tone, so it could be any note, so I just put C-sharp and D, and I kept fooling around. So when I got to the piano, 'Epistrophy', was born.
Fancy that. Is that right. Isn't that something?
And I showed it to Monk, you know.

I was hung up with (singing) -- then I was hung up for the last two bars. I couldn't figure it out, what chords would be the best. So that afternoon I came, we had rehearsal, so I showed it to Monk. I said, 'Now, right here, Monk, this is the whole tune. Now, I have six bars of the channel, with those last two bars, I can't seem to find them.' So he played it, (singing) -- he said, 'There it is.'
I said, 'Well, doggone, that's it, Monk.'
It's such an absolutely logical extension of it.
Yeah, uh-huh. So then, 'Epistrophe,' was born. And I said, 'Well, we'll take this tune and we'll each buy a home.'
The tune never made it that big.
